conversation.user: Actually, I want the hands-on DIY experience. What if I cast it in place instead?
conversation.assistant:
Switching to a cast-in-situ (cast-in-place) method gives you that classic, deeply tactile DIY experience—tamping the hemp-lime mix by hand inside your temporary formwork allows you to shape the walls directly around your timber frame. The authoritative planning volume remains **9.9 cubic metres** for your 420 square feet of wall area at a 10-inch thickness.

For a hands-on cast-in-place build, you'll need to account for building and moving temporary formwork in lifts, mixing the binder and hurds on-site, and allowing adequate drying time between lifts. Keep in mind that structural engineering plans, final local permitting, and exact material sourcing details will still need to be verified independently for your specific site.
